methodology: Individual preliminary verse screening against Hebrew Bible law and ethical motifs. Primary-text check for pig prohibition only; remaining legal comparisons require deeper contextual checks. No proof of absence or direct literary dependence.

candidates.text_witness: Masoretic Hebrew text and Revised JPS 2023 translation accessible via Sefaria
candidates.differences: Leviticus and Deuteronomy classify swine by hoof and cud criteria and prohibit touching carcasses; Qur'an 2:173 combines swine with carrion, blood, and dedication to other than God and includes an exception under compulsion.
candidates.caveat: The Hebrew prohibitions are textually checkable; broader list and necessity rule require separate passages. This does not establish textual borrowing.

candidates.text_witness: Hebrew Masoretic text and JPS translation; passage needs full context verification
candidates.similarities: Both address proportionate retaliation for injury.
candidates.differences: Exodus 21:23–25 discusses injuries in the context of a pregnant woman and legal proportionality; Qur'an 2:178 addresses homicide, categories of persons, remission and payment.
candidates.caveat: Do not present Exodus as identical homicide procedure; examine Exodus 21:12–14 and Jewish legal interpretation.

candidates.text_witness: Hebrew Masoretic text with English translation; full legal comparison pending
candidates.similarities: Both concern family property transfer upon death.
candidates.differences: Numbers sets an order of heirs when a person dies without a son; Qur'an 2:180 concerns a prescribed bequest to parents and close relatives.
candidates.caveat: A general legal context, not equivalent testamentary rule. Requires further primary-text and reception-history study.

open_questions: Compare Leviticus 17 and Deuteronomy 12 for blood and carcass rules.
Study the Arabic necessity clause in 2:173 against Jewish emergency exceptions without anachronism.
Check Exodus 21 homicide context and Numbers 27 inheritance versus wills.
